title: Verticalized prompt microbundle curation and contextual exemplar weighting for calibration
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: build a repeatable, domain-aware curation pipeline that generates compact 'microbundles' of production prompts tailored to verticals (e.g., support, billing, search, e-comm) for FP8/INT8 quantization calibration and downstream accuracy validation. These microbundles should capture typical context-length distributions, core intents, and tail failure modes so calibration profiles produce stable accuracy across customer workloads.
background: Current calibration packs are large and domain-agnostic which dilutes signal for vertical-specific degradations after aggressive quantization. We also lack a principled exemplar weighting scheme that balances recency, rarity, and token-length distribution for tight microbundles required by customers that want per-vertical validators.
sampling_algorithm: Hybrid pipeline: 1) vertical assignment using existing domain classifier (confidence threshold 0.6); 2) stratify by context-length buckets (0-64,65-256,257-1024,>1024 tokens) to preserve kernel execution profiles; 3) reservoir sampling per bucket with decay factor alpha=0.85 to bias recent traffic; 4) anomaly-boost: incorporate 1% of samples flagged by production anomaly detector (errors, hallucinations, high latency); 5) tail-intent oversample multiplier x3 for intent classes with <1% frequency; 6) final exemplar weighting uses priority scores (recency*0.6 + rarity*0.3 + latency_signal*0.1) and selects top-N per vertical where N is tuned by quant target (FP8: N=800-1200, INT8: N=2000-3500).
tradeoffs_and_risks: Smaller microbundles speed validation but risk missing rare failure modes. Decay-weighting improves recency alignment at the cost of historical stability. Vertical assignment errors will leak examples between packs; mitigation: holdout cross-check against manual label set. Oversampling tails improves sensitivity to regressions but can inflate false-positive alerts during automated regression sweeps.
experiment_plan: Phase 1 (week 1-2): implement sampler and generate microbundles for 6 target verticals using 30 days of anonymized prod traffic. Phase 2 (week 3-4): run quantization calibration for FP8 and INT8 profiles using existing compile/runner; collect token-level and sequence-level metrics. Phase 3 (week 5): A/B validate on holdout real-traffic replay for two tenants (support-heavy and e-comm). Phase 4 (week 6): iterate sampling hyperparams and produce final packs and docs.
success_metrics: (a) Per-vertical sequence-level accuracy delta vs fp32 <= 2 percentage points for primary intent accuracy (FP8 target) and <=3 percentage points for INT8; (b) Token-level KL divergence threshold per vertical < 0.12; (c) Microbundle coverage: packs cover >=95% of high-frequency intents and >=80% of error-prone examples flagged historically; (d) Calibration runtime: generate pack + calibrate profile in <4 hours for FP8 and <8 hours for INT8 on dedicated infra.
acceptance_criteria: 1) Pipeline can produce reproducible microbundles for 6 verticals with N adjustable via config. 2) Calibration runs complete and produce quant profiles that meet per-vertical thresholds in success_metrics on validation harness. 3) Documentation and runbook committed to Confluence with example commands. 4) Code reviewed and merged, with infra runbook for scheduled re-curation every 30 days.

Coordinate with privacy team to ensure anonymization thresholds for example retention. Discuss whether to store microbundles as compressed JSONL with salted IDs for customer-specific variants.
